<Subject 2> (appears throughout as the only setting): fully_preserved - every visible background element matches <Picture 2>: pavilion, corridors, courtyard, rockery pond, willow, and mist. The location of <Video 1> is not preserved, not partially preserved, and not weakly referenced.

detailed_description:
The target video uses the character of <Picture 1> and the garden of <Picture 2> only. Duration is 10 seconds. Framing is medium close-up: <Subject 1> from about the waist up, with head, torso, arms, and hands visible.
[Shot 1] A medium close-up holds <Subject 1> centered, waist-up. Face, hair, clothing, and proportions stay locked to the three-view <Picture 1> through every head turn and shoulder rotation. The performer from <Video 1> is not shown and is not used as a body double. Behind <Subject 1>, the only background is <Subject 2> from <Picture 2>: out-of-focus but readable red-lacquer pavilion and carved corridors with grey flying eaves, stone paving, mossy rockery and pond, a drooping willow, and light mist under golden-hour light. Lighting on skin and clothing matches <Picture 2>. No architecture, landscape, waterfront, or extra people from <Video 1> appear in any frame. <Subject 1> dances by retargeting <Video 1>'s kinematics onto this body: the same beat timing, torso sway, arm arcs, hand gestures, and head turns, adapted to <Picture 1>'s proportions. The visible dance is the upper-body result of that retarget, not a newly invented routine. Hair and clothing follow those accents. The camera stays medium close-up for all 10 seconds, keeping <Subject 1> centered in <Subject 2>. It makes only slight pan, tilt, or drift following an arm rise, a head turn, or a torso lean, then settles. It does not copy <Video 1>'s camera, does not cut, does not tighten to a close-up, and does not pull out to full body. The dance ends on the matching final pose at 00:10.000, still <Subject 1> from <Picture 1> standing in the garden from <Picture 2>.
